subject: Cloud Computing
title: The SolarWinds Supply Chain Attack
description: A fast breakdown of The SolarWinds Supply Chain Attack for builders.

hook.text: Russian hackers injected malware into SolarWinds' software update. 18,000 organizations installed it unknowingly.

buildup.text: SolarWinds Orion monitored IT infrastructure for government agencies and Fortune 500 companies worldwide.

discovery.text: The compromised update gave attackers access to networks at the U.S. Treasury and Homeland Security.

twist.text: The attack went undetected for nine months. Attackers moved through cloud environments, reading emails and files.

climax.text: SolarWinds changed how the world thinks about software supply chains. Trust in third-party tools can never be assumed.

punchline.text: One trusted update. Nine months undetected. Global damage.

quiz.question: How long did the SolarWinds attack go undetected?
options: It was detected immediately but took months to fix
The attack lasted only 24 hours before being stopped

details.summary: In 2020, attackers compromised SolarWinds' build system and inserted a backdoor into an Orion software update distributed to 18,000 organizations including US government agencies. The attack went undetected for months, demonstrating devastating supply chain risk.
details.whyItMatters: SolarWinds showed that trusted software updates can become attack vectors. It reshaped how organizations evaluate supply chain security for cloud and infrastructure tools.
takeaways: A build system compromise inserted a backdoor into updates
The attack remained undetected for months

faq.question: How was the SolarWinds attack discovered?
faq.answer: FireEye detected the intrusion when investigating a breach of their own systems. They traced the attack back to a compromised SolarWinds Orion update and disclosed the findings publicly, triggering a massive industry-wide investigation.

faq.question: How can supply chain attacks be prevented?
faq.answer: Verify software signatures, maintain a software bill of materials, monitor build pipelines for tampering, use binary analysis on updates, segment network access for monitoring tools, and implement zero-trust principles that limit what any single software can access.
